name: Men's Class B blue long-sleeve shirt, tie and trousers (nametag position only)
size_basis: Silhouette (long sleeves, collar, torso, trousers/skirt) measured from CAPR 39-1 Figure 4.8 (3 March 2020): the figure was rendered at 2.2x, traced, and scaled with the registration of its short-sleeve twin to the short-sleeve base image, so interior parts line up with garment-blues-class-b-shirt-male. No real garment was measured. Then the whole sheet is scaled by 1.2171 (LIVE-ART2 item 1; 0.0474 in/px becomes 0.0577): the men's pocket measures 4.31 in wide on the traced image, and a USAF-style men's size-M short-sleeve shirt pocket is about 5.25 in wide x 6 in tall (ESTIMATE: AF shirt pattern dimension supplied with the task, no CAPR 39-1 or DAFI 36-2903 dimension; the CAPR 39-1 Fig 4.9 nametag (3 3/8 in) read as a ruler gives a smaller 4.56 in, the figure is schematic), so K = 5.25 / 4.313. The pocket is drawn 5.25 x 6.0 in, flap 2.02 in deep. Nameplate, epaulet strap width, buttons and strokes stay true size.

collar_honor_guard.how_hidden: the group carries display="none" in the file; to wear it remove that attribute (or draw it with display inline)
collar_honor_guard.hides_note: the closed collar (group collar-foreground) and the tie or tab; nothing else
collar_honor_guard.polygons: collar_honor_guard_right / _left are the leaf pieces [top end, collar point, inner end, revers corner, break, apex] (viewer-left first, the sheets' own naming: right = the wearer's right); collar_honor_guard_open_neck is the V (the neck arc, then the apex); collar_honor_guard_roll_right / _left are the V's sides sampled from the top end to the apex

landmarks_note: rects are {x,y,w,h}; polygons are [[x,y]...]; all in user units (0.01 in), origin top-left of the artwork box; sleeve_flat_view {left:{x,y},right:{x,y}} is where the top_center of the flat sleeve assets <id>-sleeve-flat-left / -right sits beside the figure (outboard of each arm, its top at the shoulder seam height, 1 in clear of the sleeve outline; it lies outside this artwork box) | honor guard: collar_honor_guard_* polygons and polylines are the honor guard collar state (group collar-honor-guard), [[x,y]...] in user units; collar_insignia_honor_guard_right / _left are the vertex means of its two leaf pieces (the same rule as collar_insignia_right / _left)

epaulet_strap.edge_on: LIVE10-ART 2: drawn edge-on like the Class A board strip: a band edge_thickness_in thick, its upper edge the shoulder line, its outer end the armhole seam, the point and the button foreshortened across it; width_in is the strap's TRUE width (the top view's)

measured.figure: CAPR 39-1 Fig 4.8 (men's long-sleeve figure) at this sheet's scale (x 0.03664, y 0.03299 in/px, make-long-outlines.js)
measured.photo: images/base/lt_col_blues_class_b_male.webp edge-on strip 117 px = 5.1 in at the 5.25 in pocket scale, slope 21 deg

epaulet_strap.note: the strap lies along the shoulder line N-SP of the finished silhouette (dimensions.finishing), its upper edge IS that line, its outer end is the armhole seam, a band 0.46 in thick (LIVE10-ART 2; the true strap is 1.0 in wide as commit 72a36ce9); the button 1/2 in from the tip is the brief's value, no figure shows it under the sleeve; the sheet's whole shoulder line is 5.93 in

tie.source: LIVE9-ART 1: the numbers of the Class A coat sheet's own tie (make-blues-a.js, tie.js): knot 1.81 in wide, its shoulder 0.784 in below the apex, neck 1.00 in wide at 1.643 in and 1.13 in at 2.004 in, blade 2.24 in wide at 4.577 in; below that the blade widens to 3.0 in across (Fig 4.8 at the belt) over the rest of its length; the tip at 80 % of the buckle height (4.1.8.3). The apex is the collar junction J.

collar.source: B2 (Ethan, 2026-11-10: "the collar between the aviator shirt and class b should be the same. transfer the shape of the aviator to the class b, just changing the color"): the same drawing as the aviator shirt's (base-art/shirt-collar.js, the code make-aviator.js builds it with: AVIATOR-ART, LIVE8-ART 1, LIVE12-ART 1), in this shirt's colours: the leaf cloth is the shirt's, the leaf edge the outline's navy at half strength, the inside of the collar band the aviator's two shades taken from the shirt cloth. The collar's top (the apex of the back of the collar) is where this sheet's own neck began; the junction (the aviator's Q, 2.60 in below the collar's top on the men's, 2.45 in on the women's) is where the knot's / tab's apex sits. Same estimate as the aviator's: no regulation dimension.

finishing.note: shoulder line straightened between the neck vertex and the shoulder point, armhole seam from the shoulder point to the armpit apex, hem hook / gap bulge removed (finishShoulderArmpit)

scale.note: pocket 5.25 x 6 in = USAF-style men's size-M short-sleeve shirt (estimate); the whole sheet scaled so the traced pocket width equals it

sleeve_widening.note: outward warp of the sleeve between the armhole seam and the outer edge (seam, body, shoulder and straps unmoved) so the true-size 3 1/2 in chevron lies between the outline and the armhole seam; an estimate, the regulation gives no sleeve width
sleeve_widening.chevron_fit_note: clearance in inches from every row of the 3 1/2 in chevron, placed as the engine does (visual centre on chevron_halfway, turned along shoulder_seam to elbow), to the outer edge and to the armhole seam; positive = on the sleeve. The women's 4 in option (4.1.12.2.3.3, the 3 1/2 in art scaled to 4.00 x 6.54 in) is listed under 4 and still overhangs, clipped to the silhouette by the engine

lower_body.kind: trousers fill the body from the waist line to the cut line, and the belt strap runs from one side edge of the body to the other
lower_body.note: LIVE13-ART 49 (Ethan, 2026-11-12: "both the belt and pants must go all the way around ... theres light blue all the way around"): a tucked-in shirt ends at the belt, so from the belt down the whole body is the lower garment. It was cut by the colour profile of the regulation figure (bottoms), which is narrower than the body: shirt cloth showed beside the belt and beside the trousers down to the hem. Now the cloth's edge is the body's side edge, read from the sheet's own outline (the central span of every 0.04 in row of the outline with its armpit gaps), and the outline clips it; the arm stays on top because the cloth stops at the arm's edge. The waist line, the belt rows, the cut line, the buckle and everything above the waist line are as before.

top_edge.note: the same parabola as before (through the old half width and the centre line's sag), carried out to the body's edge; the middle of the edge renders pixel for pixel as before

belt_strap.note: a rectangle whose half width reaches the body's edge on every one of its rows and stops inside the armpit gap, short of the arm; the sheet's outline clips it at the body's edge, so the strap, its edge lines and its stitching run from one edge to the other (it was the figure's trouser width, short of the edge)

sides.clip: clipSil (the sheet's outline, even-odd: the gaps beside the body are holes); the cloth runs at most 0.03 in into a gap so that the clip makes the edge

arm_inner_edge.note: the men's long sleeve lies on the body from the lower end of the armpit gap down to the cuff, so there the body's edge is the arm's inner edge: the straight line from the closure of the gap (its lowest point) to the cuff band's inner end, then down the cuff's inner edge to the outline (the line continues the slope of the gap's body-side edge, about 0.18 in per in)

lower_body.source: the sheet's own outline (measured from CAPR 39-1 Fig 4.8, make-long-outlines.js), as the sheet has it; no new measurement of the garment

collar_honor_guard.kind: the sheet's own collar worn open and laid back as the Honor Guard guidance draws its Class B figures (CAPR 39-1 9.6, the guidance's page 4); one drawing for the short and the long sheet of the cut (computed from the short sheet's collar, registered at each sheet's top ends and centre front)
collar_honor_guard.source: "CAP Honor Guard Uniform Guidance", page 4, the Class B short-sleeve and long-sleeve figures at 6x, 33.4 px/in (the four buttons 449.5 px = the sheet's 13.44 in); short and long figures agree within 0.1 in on every point

scale_to_sheet.rule: every figure length (x and y) times k = this sheet's half distance between the top ends / the figure's 3.14 in; the break is the everyday collar's own (on the placket, at the first button)

geometry_in.note: x from the centre front, y down from the top ends; the left-hand (viewer) front is the over front

roll_line.limit: the bow stops where the curve would leave the top end outward (control point x <= top end x)
roll_line.note: cubic top end -> apex, both control points `bow` in outside the chord

patch.note: clearance = from the patch's alpha edge to the centre line of each roll line, least over the edge (negative = the patch overlaps the leaf); with the figure's own bow the patch only grazes the line (men) or overlaps it (women): the figure draws its patch 3.23 in across, ours is 3.0, and the sheet's collar sits closer to its first button

collar_honor_guard.anchors: collar_insignia_honor_guard_right / _left, collar_honor_guard_apex, collar_honor_guard_patch_center (the everyday collar_insignia_* and the cap seat are unchanged)
estimated: the sheet's break is the everyday one (the sheet's placket and first button), not scaled from the figure
the roll lines' extra bow, which only exists so the patch clears them

documented: light blue long-sleeve shirt, two pleated pockets, convertible cuffs, epaulets (CAPR 39-1 4.1.11.1.1)
long sleeves end 1/4 to 1/2 in below the wrist (4.1.11.1.1)
tie: the tip covers a portion of the belt buckle but does not extend below it (4.1.8.3, as for the other men's blues)
nameplate centred on, resting on (not over) the top edge of the wearer's right pocket (4.1.11.1.1.2.1)
cadet NCOs/airmen: metal chevrons on both sides of the collar, 1 in from and parallel to the front of the collar (4.1.11.1.1.1.4)
assumed: px-to-inch scale (0.0474 in/px x K, K from the 5.25 in pocket width, an estimate)
nameplate size (3.375 x 0.75 in = Vanguard CAP0599M cadet name plate (blue plastic, 3 3/8 x 3/4 in); no dimension in CAPR 39-1 or DAFI 36-2903; no dimension in CAPR 39-1 or DAFI 36-2903)

epaulet strap drawn on the sheet from the shoulder line, edge-on: a band 0.46 in thick (the true strap is 1.0 in wide), 0.5 in point, button 1/2 in from the tip (the brief's value) foreshortened across the band, one line of topstitch 0.09 in in (dimensions.epaulet_strap)
pocket and seam geometry read off the base image
collar leaves: the Class A coat's closed collar construction, leading edge about 3 in, an estimate (dimensions.collar)
shirt, trouser/skirt and line colours sampled from the base image
sleeve widening: the sleeve is drawn wider than the traced hanging view (CFG.widen, dimensions.sleeve_widening)
belt strap colour #14347f (and its #7d95d6 stitching) is a choice, not sampled: the base image paints the belt the same navy as the trousers; regulation says only blue belt (4.1.11.1.1.5, 4.1.12.7)
trousers cut off at the base image's crop line
